name: fuzz_get_first_tlv_basic
reasoning: Targets TLV parsing with an intentionally incomplete bounds check before reading tlv->value[tlv->length-1], enabling KLEE to detect out-of-bounds read (CWE-125) and pointer arithmetic overflow issues.

name: fuzz_get_next_tlv_step
reasoning: Exercises advancing the TLV cursor and an unchecked access to the last byte of the value, which can cause out-of-bounds read (CWE-125) when the claimed length exceeds the remaining buffer.

name: fuzz_setup_http_post_overflow
reasoning: Triggers integer overflow (CWE-190) when computing allocation size and then out-of-bounds write (CWE-787) via memcpy using tlv->length larger than the allocated buffer.

name: fuzz_add_mime_part_oob
reasoning: Copies attacker-controlled length into a fixed-size buffer without bounds checking to expose buffer overflow (CWE-787).

name: fuzz_parse_mime_tlv_divzero
reasoning: Explicitly exercises a divide-by-zero (CWE-369) path inside a secondary parser function for MIME-related TLVs.

name: fuzz_open_socket_addrlen_oob
reasoning: Over-reads user-provided address bytes based on untrusted addrlen leading to out-of-bounds read (CWE-125) and potential stack overflow if addrlen is large (CWE-121/CWE-787).

name: fuzz_sockopt_callback_index_oob
reasoning: Directly indexes a small local array with attacker-controlled socket value causing out-of-bounds write (CWE-787) and potentially negative index underflow (CWE-191/CWE-823).

name: fuzz_select_bitset_oob
reasoning: Expands bit indices beyond the fixed-size fd_set, leading to out-of-bounds writes in the bitset array (CWE-787).

name: fuzz_set_allowed_protocols_oob
reasoning: Writes into an options[] array using an unbounded index derived from attacker-controlled input, exposing out-of-bounds write (CWE-787) and possible write-what-where condition (CWE-123).

name: fuzz_initialize_fuzz_data_copy_oob
reasoning: Demonstrates two bugs: fixed-size buffer overflow when copying initialization data (CWE-121/CWE-787) and heap overflow when copying data_len bytes into a too-small allocation based on the first byte (CWE-787/CWE-190).
